title: The Midnight Meeting and the Famous Verse
paragraphs: So, there was this guy named Nicodemus, a super important religious leader (a Pharisee) among the Jewish people. One night, pretty late, he came to visit Jesus. He said, "Rabbi, we all know you're a teacher sent directly from God. Nobody could do all these amazing, God-revealing things you're doing unless God was totally with you."
Jesus replied, "You're spot on. Seriously, listen up: Unless someone is 'born from above,' they can't even begin to understand what I'm talking about—they can't see God's kingdom."

Nicodemus was totally confused. "How can anyone be born again once they're already grown up? You can't just climb back into your mom's womb! What are you even talking about with this 'born from above' thing?"

Jesus said, "You're not really listening. Let me break it down again. Unless a person totally gives in to this original creation—you know, like when the 'wind hovered over the water' at the very beginning, the invisible stuff moving the visible stuff, a kind of baptism into a brand new life—it's impossible to actually enter God's kingdom. When you look at a baby, it's just a body you can see and touch. But the real person taking shape inside is formed by something you can't see or touch—that's the Spirit—and that's what makes them a living spirit."

"So, don't be so shocked when I tell you that you've got to be 'born from above'—like, out of this world, if that makes sense. You totally get how the wind blows wherever it wants. You can hear it rustling through the trees, but you have no clue where it came from or where it's going next. That's exactly how it is for everyone who is 'born from above' by the wind of God, the Spirit of God."
Nicodemus asked, "Wait, what do you even mean by this? How does any of this actually happen?"

Jesus responded, "You're a respected teacher in Israel, and you don't even know these basic things? Listen carefully. I'm telling you the honest truth. I'm only talking about what I know firsthand, from my own experience; I'm only testifying to what I've seen with my own eyes. There's no secondhand info here, no rumors. Yet, instead of just looking at the evidence and accepting it, you're just stalling with questions. If I tell you things that are super obvious, right in front of your face, and you don't believe me, what's the point of telling you about things you can't see, the deep things of God?"

"Nobody has ever gone up into God's presence except the One who came down from that Presence, the Son of Man. It's like how Moses lifted up the bronze snake in the desert so people could look at it and believe they'd be healed (Numbers 21:8-9). In the same way, the Son of Man has to be lifted up— and everyone who looks up to him, truly trusting and expecting, will get a real life, an eternal life."

"Here's how much God totally loved the world: He gave his Son, his one and only Son. And this is why: so that no one ever has to be destroyed; by believing in him, anyone can have a complete and lasting life. God didn't go through all that trouble of sending his Son just to point fingers and tell the world how messed up it was. He came to help, to fix the world up again. Anyone who trusts in him is declared innocent; anyone who refuses to trust him has actually been under a death sentence for a long time without even realizing it. And why? Because that person failed to believe in the one-of-a-kind Son of God when they were introduced to him."

"This is the major crisis we're facing: God's light streamed into the world, but people everywhere just ran for the darkness. They chose the darkness because they weren't genuinely interested in making God happy. Everyone who constantly does evil, who's hooked on denial and living in an illusion, hates God's light and won't come anywhere near it, scared of being painfully exposed. But anyone who works and lives in truth and reality totally welcomes God's light so that their work can be seen for the God-work it truly is."

After this whole conversation, Jesus went with his disciples into the Judean countryside and hung out with them there. He was also baptizing people. At the same time, John (the Baptist) was also baptizing over at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there. This was all happening before John got thrown into jail. John's disciples actually got into a big argument with some of the religious leaders (the establishment Jews) about what baptism really meant. So, they went to John and said, "Rabbi, you know that guy who was with you on the other side of the Jordan? The one you vouched for with your testimony? Well, he's basically competing with us now. He's baptizing too, and everyone is going to him instead of us!"

John answered, "It's just not possible for a person to succeed—and I'm talking about real, eternal success—without help from heaven. You yourselves were right there when I publicly announced that I wasn't the Messiah but simply the one sent ahead of him to get things ready. The guy who gets the bride is, by definition, the bridegroom. And the bridegroom's friend, his 'best man'—that's me—standing right there by his side where he can hear every word, is genuinely thrilled. How could he possibly be jealous when he knows the wedding is happening and the marriage is off to a great start?"
"That's why my cup is overflowing with joy. This is the exact moment for him to move into the spotlight, while I quietly step off to the sidelines."

"The One who comes from above is way above all other messengers from God. Someone born on earth is limited to earth and speaks earth-language; but the One born from heaven is in a league of his own. He lays out the proof of what he saw and heard in heaven. But seriously, no one really wants to deal with these facts. Yet, anyone who truly examines this evidence will eventually stake their whole life on this: that God himself is the truth."

"The One that God sent speaks God's actual words. And don't think for a second that he rations out the Spirit in tiny bits and pieces. The Father loves the Son like crazy, extravagantly. He handed everything over to him so he could give it away—a super generous distribution of gifts. That's why whoever accepts and trusts the Son gets in on everything, a life that's complete and lasts forever! And that's also why the person who avoids and distrusts the Son is totally in the dark and doesn't see life. All they experience of God is darkness, and a really angry darkness at that."
